title: Beyond Static Interpretability: Anticipating Post-SFT Mechanisms from Pre-SFT Parameters for Better Tuning
abstract: arXiv:2608.24482v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Mechanistic Localization bridges mechanistic interpretability and post-training optimization by isolating critical parameters via interpretative approaches and then guiding parameter-efficient Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) in a ``locating-then-tuning'' paradigm. However, due to the retrospective nature of mechanistic interpretability, directly interpreting pre-SFT models introduces misleading conclusions. Specifically for novel tasks, initially identified neurons differ drastically from those governing the final model, introducing biases that actively disrupt SFT. To address this, we propose a forward-looking localization framework that accurately estimates the post-SFT interpretability state using only pre-SFT parameters and the target dataset. Theoretically, we model SFT as a continuous parameter evolution, leveraging Taylor expansion to rigorously bridge the post-tuning mechanistic objective with the pre-SFT model's dynamic gradients

translated_title: 超越静态可解释性：从预SFT参数预测后SFT机制以优化微调
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24482v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：机制定位通过可解释方法隔离关键参数，然后以“定位-再微调”范式指导参数高效的监督微调（SFT），从而桥接机制可解释性与后训练优化。然而，由于机制可解释性的回顾性本质，直接解释预SFT模型会引入误导性结论。特别是对于新任务，最初识别的神经元与最终模型控制的神经元差异巨大，引入的偏差会主动干扰SFT。为解决此问题，我们提出一个前瞻性定位框架，仅使用预SFT参数和目标数据集，准确估计后SFT的可解释性状态。理论上，我们将SFT建模为连续参数演化，利用泰勒展开严格桥接微调后的机制目标与预SFT模型的动态梯度。
tldr: 本文提出一种前瞻性定位框架，仅基于预SFT参数和目标数据集预测后SFT的机制状态，避免了传统静态可解释性带来的偏差，从而优化监督微调过程。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a forward-looking localization framework that predicts post-SFT mechanistic states using only pre-SFT parameters and the target dataset, avoiding biases from static interpretability to optimize supervised fine-tuning.
